ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening of every shareholder, director, manager, authorized representative and ultimate beneficial owner against the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council sanctions lists, the Luxembourg national PEP database and the CSSF warning list. Positive PEP hits trigger enhanced due diligence requiring senior management approval, documented source of funds, source of wealth, and a written EDD file. Because the scope is ISIC 7020 government affairs and lobbying, the compliance file must also address potential political-exposure risk and corruption red flags.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official company-law languages are French, German and Luxembourgish. The name must be entered in the RCS using Latin characters; non-Latin scripts require an official transliteration into French, German or English. The legal name must be preceded or followed by 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' and must not be confusingly similar to an existing RCS name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (when used as a leading name implying state authority)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the applicant may resubmit a corrected name within 15 days and, where applicable, apply to the competent minister for authorization of sensitive terms. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant must file a formal administrative appeal with the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within one month of notification and may request an interim suspension of the rejection while the appeal is pending. Legal counsel must ensure the final name is published and recorded exactly as approved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A mail-drop or virtual office alone does not satisfy the statutory requirement that a SARL have a registered office in Luxembourg. Use of an approved domiciliation agent is permissible only if the company maintains genuine management presence, decision-making activity and, for government-affairs lobbying, a physical Luxembourg establishment. A purely paper office will not satisfy the UBO, tax substance or AML/CFT expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection for a compliant SARL in this high-stakes government-affairs advisory sector; the risk rises materially if the company relies on virtual office arrangements, has inconsistent employee substance, or triggers adverse PEP/sanctions alerts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Companies Act of 10 August 1915, as consolidated and amended, in particular Title V (Articles 109 to 216) governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (S.à r.l.); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA); relevant notarial provisions of the Civil Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), filed through a Luxembourg civil-law notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) containing the articles of association (statuts), filed electronically by the notary with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The S.à r.l. requires minimum issued capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed. At formation, at least 25% of the nominal value of each subscribed share must be paid in cash; cash contributions are deposited in a Luxembourg bank account in the name of the company in formation and confirmed by a bank certificate to the notary. Contributions in kind require full payment at incorporation and an independent valuation report. No state-run escrow account is required; the notary and bank certificate serve as the verification mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [NAME] S.À R.L.
(a) The share capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed by the undersigned shareholders, and each share is taken as paid to the minimum legal extent, evidenced by the bank certificate.
(b) The registered office is fixed at [full address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the competent authorities are notified.
(c) The initial manager is appointed: [Full Name], who shall sign all registration documents, open bank accounts, and represent the company until replaced.
(d) The manager is authorized to file the notarial deed with the RCS and to take all ancillary actions.
Resolved unanimously and entered into the minute book this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal name availability and pre-incorporation compliance screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via myguichet.lu and RCS Online; Luxembourg notary pre-filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name availability check through the RCS electronic portal or instruct the notary to reserve the proposed name. Verify distinctive character and absence of conflict with existing corporate names or reserved trademarks. Formally reserve the approved S.à r.l. name and retain the reservation reference for use in the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each proposed shareholder
Passport or national ID of each proposed manager
Signed engagement letter with Luxembourg counsel or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as misleading, indistinguishable, or conflicting, select a new name and immediately reapply; the failed reservation is released and does not create a negative record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of statutory documents and opening the capital holding account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary and a qualifying Luxembourg credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the articles of association (statuts) consistent with the approved corporate purpose. Concurrently, the bank opens a blocked or non-disbursement account in the name of the company in formation and receives the minimum paid-up portion of the EUR 12,000 capital. The bank issues a certificate of payment or blocked-funds confirmation for delivery to the notary.
required_dossiers: Identity documents for shareholders and managers
Beneficial ownership and shareholding structure details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests clarification of source of funds, provide source-of-wealth evidence; if statutory clauses are questioned, the notary amends the draft and a correspondingly updated bank certificate is obtained before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the incorporation deed and RCS pre-validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary, member of the Chamber of Notaries; RCS electronic pre-validation channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The shareholders or their lawful proxies appear before the notary for signature of the notarial deed. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, capital payment certificate, powers of attorney, and the lawful business purpose. After signature, the notary submits the draft for RCS pre-validation and confirms the reserved name.
required_dossiers: Duly executed powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS pre-validation identifies a formal or legal defect, the notary prepares and executes a corrective deed (acte rectificatif) before the same notary and resubmits to RCS within the applicable deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final electronic registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers, through the notary's e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the signed notarial deed, the statutory articles, declarations of legal representatives, registered office evidence, and the bank certificate. The official RCS registration fee is paid. The RCS issues the company registration number and the RCS extract. The registration date establishes the company's legal existence and third-party enforceability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises observations, the notary files a corrected page or supplementary addendum to the same dossier within the rectification period, normally 15 days, preserving the original filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and tax, VAT and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers; Administration des contributions directes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the deed is published in the RESA. The company receives its Luxembourg 13-digit national identification number. If taxable activities are carried out, submit the VAT registration application to the AED. If employees will be hired, register as an employer with the CCSS and enrol officers for social security coverage where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the articles of association
Mandate for tax representative if non-resident
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or VAT registration is delayed, file a remedial registration application through myguichet.lu using the RCS extract and request voluntary disclosure to minimise any late-filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance records, bank account activation and interest-representative registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management; Luxembourg notary; designated transparency register for interest representatives; commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first managers' meeting to approve the formation resolutions, adopt the initial minutes, and open the corporate records, including the share register and statutory filings. Activate the operational bank account once the RCS extract is available. If the company will contact Luxembourg public officials for lobbying or government affairs, complete the mandatory registration in the interest-representative transparency register before substantive lobbying activities commence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the transparency register application is queried, provide the requested contact and engagement details, adjust the internal public-affairs protocol, and maintain an activity log until the registration is confirmed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction des classes moyennes; Luxembourg Business Registers for interest-representative transparency registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or manufacturing permit applies to ISIC 7020 government affairs advisory. The mandatory authorization is the Interest Representative Transparency Registration (Registre des représentants d'intérêts) together with the corporate administrative licence obtained through RCS incorporation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C. The proposed use is exclusively office-based consultancy and does not trigger a full EIA report or environmental registration under the Luxembourg Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC-emitting processes, or hazardous waste streams are generated. Discharge is limited to sanitary wastewater connected to the municipal sewer under commune acceptance. Solid waste must be sorted and collected by licensed operators. Any future fit-out must comply with EU energy performance and indoor air quality standards applicable to offices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance must be obtained through the communal fire safety officer and the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours for the leased premises. Structural load certification is provided by the municipal building authority under the granted occupancy permit. Workplace compliance clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) is required for office layout, emergency exits, electrical installations, ventilation, lighting, and accessibility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTVA) for VAT and registration duties; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / RCS) for commercial registration and corporate TIN issuance. Main digital portals: MyGuichet.lu, e-TVA (AEDTVA), eCDF (ACD) and LBR.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL by notarial deed (or deed executed before a notary) with a minimum subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000. Step 2: File the incorporation file with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and obtain the RCS registration number and the 13-digit national identification number (matricule), which serves as the statutory corporate TIN for direct tax purposes. Step 3: Request VAT registration with the AEDTVA through MyGuichet.lu (Form 102) once annual taxable turnover exceeds EUR 25,000, or earlier where the SARL carries out intra-EU acquisitions above EUR 10,000 per year, receives reverse-charge services, or makes supplies of services or goods that are taxable in Luxembourg; upon approval the AEDTVA issues the LU VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits). Step 4: Register the SARL with the ACD for corporate income tax and net wealth tax and with the competent communal administration for municipal business tax, and set up the electronic filing profile (monthly or quarterly VAT via e-TVA, annual CIT return via eCDF). Step 5: File the annual corporate income tax return with the ACD, usually by 31 December of the following financial year, with extensions available upon request.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; the SARL is classified by legal form as a fully taxable resident corporate entity (subject to CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax on worldwide income). Available statutory elections: (1) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Art. 164bis LIR, requiring a 95% direct or indirect holding committed for at least five years and a joint election filed with the ACD; (2) VAT grouping election allowing closely-linked Luxembourg-established persons to be treated as a single taxable person; (3) advance tax rulings from the ACD on participation exemption (Art. 166 LIR), financing, hybrid-mismatch and cross-border restructuring affairs; (4) choice of an accounting reference period other than the calendar year with the corresponding CIT and VAT filing calendar; (5) ATAD and hybrid-mismatch documentation elections to be supported in the CIT file.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank; exchange-control supervision is also framed by national implementation of EU capital-movement rules under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and by the Luxembourg financial-sector laws administered with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full euro-area member with unrestricted current and capital account convertibility. There is no exchange-control licensing, no mandatory conversion, and no central-bank pre-authorisation for profit remittances. Profit distribution by a Luxembourg SARL is instead subject to ordinary corporate law: annual accounts approval and the net-assets distribution test under the Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, and to company solvency rules. For a government-affairs and lobbying entity, remittances to foreign clients or shareholders must also pass AML diligence and economic-substance controls; BoP statistical reporting to the BCL may be required when cross-border flows exceed the reporting threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The Luxembourg legal order imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no statutory conversion ratio, and no foreign-exchange repatriation obligation. Export receipts, service fees and retainer income may be retained in EUR or in the invoiced currency. The only relevant obligations are transfer-pricing documentation for connected parties, VAT and invoicing rules, and the need to identify the purpose of inbound funds for BCL statistical purposes and for the bank's AML screening.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium_Feasible_With_Restrictions. A Luxembourg SARL may validly open payment accounts at an EEA-authorised electronic-money institution operating under the PSD2 passport, but such accounts are secondary rails, not statutory bank accounts. Offshore EMIs located outside the EEA cannot provide reliable treasury, escrow or lending services to a Luxembourg regulated-risk company; they also fail the CSSF's expectations for a client's first credit institution. For a government-affairs and lobbying entity, the primary account must remain with a Luxembourg or EU credit institution because the AML and fitness checks, withholdings, currency clearing and capital-blocking functions require a deposit-taking bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: High. In standard Luxembourg corporate-onboarding practice, at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner must physically attend a compliance interview at the bank's premises in Luxembourg or, exceptionally, before a Luxembourg notary or correspondent bank recognised by the Luxembourg bank. During the interview the bank records the business purpose, source of funds, expected payment volumes, beneficiary structure, sanctions status and the nature of the government-relations segment. Remote onboarding is possible only where the Luxembourg bank has an accepted video-identification procedure and is comfortable with the enhanced-risk profile; given the ISIC 7020 government-affairs and lobbying sector, most credit institutions require a first physical visit and will not rely solely on third-party remote verification for an entity with non-EU owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-sector red flag: future lobbying and public-affairs advice classified as higher-corruption-risk, with payments possibly referencing government procurement or officials.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed retainer and engagement letters setting out fixed or time-based fees and prohibiting contingent success fees; an anti-corruption and gifts policy; the Luxembourg and EU interest-representation or transparency-register filings; an organisational chart with no disguised delegation of discretionary lobbying powers; training records and an outside-counsel opinion confirming compliance with foreign-corruption statutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity, nominee shareholder structures, or non-EU UBOs with high net worth and complex residence status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RBE excerpt proving the registered beneficial owners; a shareholder register with full identification; an explaining corporate-chart memorandum; deed of incorporation and articles of association; global-register extracts for any parent; certified passports, residency proof and tax identification numbers for all UBOs; a source-of-wealth letter where the opening deposit exceeds the bank's threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds deficiency: first tranche of paid capital or a retainer prepayment arises from a third-party family office, trust or a government-related entity without clear contractual nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the payor for the past six to twelve months; a board resolution approving the contribution; the fully executed retainer agreement; invoices and proof of service delivery; trust or corporate constitutive documents; a source-of-funds declaration endorsed by senior management; external legal opinion where any public official is directly or indirectly involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and correspondent-banking friction triggered by US/EU sanctions screening, especially when outbound wires are directed to non-EU beneficiaries or when names appear near politically exposed person match lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live OFAC, EU Council and BCL sanctions system outputs; a written sanctions risk policy; counterparty due-diligence files; an end-beneficiary statement for each outbound wire; an internal escalation output with the bank's compliance decision; insurance-policy confirmations, if applicable; a commitment to provide transaction-specific information under the Luxembourg AML legal framework and CSSF Circular 17/650.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders or group entities are routed by SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA currencies or by SEPA credit transfer for EUR, with an unambiguous payment message referencing the company name, the payment purpose, a board-resolution date and the capital-subscription transaction. Typical purpose codes used in the Luxembourg banking market for direct equity investments include G30 under the BPM6 classification, possibly complemented by bank-specific code CAPIN and an accepted wording such as capital increase for LU_SARL. The bank will perform source-of-funds verification and, where the subscribed capital is held in a blocking account until the statutory capital certificate is issued, require the notarized deed of amendment for the SARL and an accountant's confirmation. If the injection is in foreign currency, the bank will quote an on-shore client-sell FX conversion to EUR; the derivative or conversion contract must state the underlying equity inflow, and the resulting EUR balance is made available after good-funds confirmation and BCL BoP reporting where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements are settled through the SWIFT MT103 network for global wires, through SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments inside the EEA, and, where documentary security is requested, through a commercial irrevocable letter of credit issued by the Luxembourg bank in favour of the creditor. The compliance rule is that every wire must include a precise remittance reference, invoice number, counterparty name and business-purpose code so that the bank can complete sanctions screening, monitoring, and, where requested, final settlement in TARGET2 via Banque Centrale du Luxembourg. For a government-affairs consultancy, outflows cover staff salaries, specialist fees, travel expenses, conference dues, retained payments to research providers and, potentially, political-ethics service charges; these must all be backed by signed contracts and invoices and, if intended for a counterparty in a high-risk jurisdiction, by additional letters of instruction confirming the ultimate beneficiary and absence of sanctions circumvention.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards executed under an ISDA or Luxembourg-law master agreement with a bank authorised in Luxembourg, with the hedging underlying evidenced by a signed retainer contract and payment plan
EUR/GBP deliverable FX forwards for UK cross-border lobbying-services expenses, to be concluded only as hedge instruments
EUR/CHF deliverable FX forwards for payments to Swiss counterparties or for Swiss franc partner costs

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing less-liquid currencies where the Luxembourg bank confirms that physical delivery is impracticable, settlement being made in EUR with an arm's-length business-purpose statement
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP cross-currency swaps matched to expected retainer inflows, subject to the CRR margin framework, valuation at market terms and a written board treasury-authorisation
OTC FX options purchased solely for risk management, with no speculative short option strategy and with an EMIR margin and threshold assessment performed by the bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end; e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 750 – EUR 25,000 on directors under the amended RCS Law of 19 December 2002; court-ordered coercive fine up to EUR 250 per day of delay; strike-off (radiation d'office) from the RCS after two consecutive years of non-deposit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial owner declaration (RBE / UBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; additionally within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 500 – EUR 250,000 under the Law of 13 January 2019 on the register of beneficial owners; credit institutions, notaries and third parties must refuse transactions or services until RBE data is accurate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (CIT) and municipal business tax (MBT) return – Form 100
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the tax year; e-filing extension until 31 December of the year following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment (taxation d'office); late-payment interest of 0.6% per calendar month from the statutory due date; late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax (NWT) return – Form 101
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the tax year; e-filing extension until 31 December of the year following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment; late-payment interest of 0.6% per calendar month; late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed net wealth tax

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SARL exceeds for two consecutive financial years two of the three thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees. Audit also compulsory for CSSF-regulated entities (licence holders), public-interest entities, and parent companies exceeding consolidated thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under Articles 26–72 of the Commercial Code and the Law of 10 August 1915 (as amended), implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS optional for individual statutory accounts and mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must reconfirm its RBE beneficial-owner data within one month of the anniversary of the initial RBE filing and within one month of any change. Any transfer of SARL shares must be made and documented in writing, recorded in the Register of Members, and, if it changes control, reflected in an updated RBE filing; non-compliance invalidates the enforceability of transfers against the company and exposes the company to RBE criminal fines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées générales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,600 – 4,300 (EUR 1,500 – 4,000) per annum for registered office / domiciliation and corporate secretarial agent services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 11,000 – 22,000 (EUR 10,000 – 20,000) per annum for an independent statutory audit by a Réviseur d'Entreprises Agréé, dependent on company size and consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% headline CIT on taxable income exceeding EUR 175,000 and 15% on the first EUR 175,000 band (LIR Art. 174), plus a 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT and municipal business tax of 6.75% in Luxembourg City, producing an aggregate effective headline rate of approximately 24.94% for profits above EUR 175,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Relevant preferences: 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (LIR Arts. 166 and 166bis) subject to 10% holding or EUR 1.2M/EUR 6M acquisition-cost tests and 12-month holding period; 80% exemption for qualifying IP-derived net income reducing the effective rate on IP royalties to approximately 5%; notional interest deduction at 5.35% for fresh equity (2024); employment and regional investment tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 522 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) combining corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax, with annexes Forms 550, 552 and 536; mandatory electronic filing through the eCDF portal on MyGuichet.lu using the Luxembourg matricule and e-business passport.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual based on the statutory accounting year; four quarterly instalment prepayments in February, May, August and November.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; automatically extended to 31 December of that same following year when the return is prepared and filed through a Luxembourg registered tax adviser or certified chartered accountant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification block: Luxembourg matricule, RCS number, registered office, legal form (SARL), tax office and fiscal year for which the declaration is made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must identify a Luxembourg permanent establishment branch or registered liaison file and provide the foreign corporate registration number and home tax reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross accounting result before any tax adjustments: total German-type trade income as per the statutory balance sheet and P&L annex (Form 550), adjusted for Luxembourg GAAP and book-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg PE, enter only the Luxembourg-source commercial and professional income attributable to the PE under the authorised OECD approach, excluding foreign head-office operating income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, management fees, employee costs, rent, lobbying-related subcontractor costs, depreciation, and deductible provisions; disallowed expenses (non-deductible fees, portions of director remuneration, fines, proportional entertainment) are reversed here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct only expenses effectively connected with the Luxembourg PE; head-office recharges are deductible only if supported by an arm's-length service agreement and a functional/substance file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 22 - Participation exemptée (régime des sociétés mères)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend and capital-gain exemption claim under LIR Arts. 166/166bis: amount of qualifying dividends obtained from a subsidiary held at 10% or with an acquisition price over EUR 1.2M and held for at least 12 months; gains require the 10% or EUR 6M threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies generally claim the exemption only for income attributable to a Luxembourg PE; foreign direct investors must prove the subsidiary is subject to an equivalent corporate tax and that no anti-abuse/LOB treaty clause is triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carried forward: net operating losses from prior years carried forward under LIR Art. 114 up to the 17-year limitation period, including the effect of change-of-control anti-abuse restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg PE of a non-resident may carry forward its own attributable losses only against future Luxembourg-source results; losses of the foreign head office cannot be imported or offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 28 - Intérêts notionnels (déduction pour capital à risque)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Notional interest deduction equal to 5.35% of qualifying net equity additions made since 2016, over five years, subject to the balance-sheet asset carve-out rules of the 2019 reform.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The deduction applies only to equity actually attributable to the Luxembourg PE's book capital; deemed risk capital relating to intra-group financing transactions must be documented in the TP file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 35 - Impôt commercial communal et contribution de solidarité
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) allocated to each commune with a PE and the 7% solidarity surcharge on corporate income tax; the effective combined tax amount is carried to the assessment and payment schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must allocate the municipal tax base to the Luxembourg commune where the PE is actually operated and must declare the PE address accurately for municipal tax coding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty of EUR 250 to EUR 25,000 per return (AO Art. 173) at the discretion of the tax office; if the return is filed after formal notice, the tax authorities may issue an official default assessment carrying a 10% tax surcharge; late-payment increases of 5% and 10% apply, together with monthly interest of 0.6% (7.2% per annum), and criminal prosecution for non-filing can lead to fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic statutory dividend withholding tax of 15% (LIR Art. 97), fully exempt at source under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the non-resident corporate shareholder holds at least 10% of the SARL for at least 12 months; treaty reductions range from 0% to 15% depending on the residence country and holding structure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a current tax residence certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, provide a written beneficial-ownership declaration, and submit these along with the relevant claim forms to the Luxembourg paying agent before the dividend distribution for relief at source; where the 15% domestic WHT has already been applied, the non-resident shareholder may file a reclaim with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) within three years of the tax payment, attaching the TRC, dividend vouchers, and a statement of actual entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes a 0% withholding tax on outbound royalties and a 0% withholding tax on outbound interest (LIR Art. 98), irrespective of the recipient's residence; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive secures the 0% rate for associated EU companies with a 25% holding for at least two years; most Luxembourg tax treaties maintain a 0% rate for royalties and interest, subject to substance and beneficial-ownership conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the Luxembourg entity belongs to a group whose consolidated turnover reaches EUR 50M and whose cross-border related-party transactions, including financing, IP, or service flows, exceed EUR 100,000 in the fiscal year; Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required where the group consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750M; the Local File must be filed with the annual CIT return or upon specific request by the ACD.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the OECD-aligned transfer pricing circular (LIR Circular 56/1) and the domestic GAAR in Art. 6 AKG together with ATAD anti-abuse rules. For a government-affairs and lobbying SARL, economic substance is decisive: the company must have a real office in Luxembourg, locally resident directors or senior consultants, qualified operational staff, active management decisions taken in Luxembourg, and a documented functional and risk profile. A letterbox company that cannot demonstrate actual lobbying activity, local execution capability, payroll, and operational premises is exposed to a recharacterisation of its structure, denial of treaty benefits and participation exemption, and refusal of Luxembourg tax residence certificates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Fraud and Repeated Late Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful concealment of lobbying retainer income, booking of fictitious agent commissions, issuing or using fake invoices, deliberate non-filing of Form 522 after formal reminders, or submitting declarations containing materially false revenue and expense figures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud under AO Arts. 111 et seq. attracts fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment; the normal five-year assessment period extends to ten years for intentional omission; official default assessments carry a 10% surcharge and monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; the municipal business licence may be withdrawn under the Law of 2 September 2011.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax officers of the SARL are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, withholding tax and penalties under AO Art. 110; criminal conviction can result in imprisonment up to five years, seizure of personal assets, travel restrictions and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL operates as a letterbox entity with no Luxembourg office, no employees, no local decision-making, passive income streams, artificial intermediary role in routing third-party government-affairs fees, and de facto management exercised from a foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the domestic GAAR (Art. 6 AKG), ATAD principal-purpose test, and treaty LOB/PPT clauses: transactions are recharacterised, the participation exemption and dividend WHT relief are denied, profits are recomputed at arm's length, a 10% tax surcharge is added, and tax residence certificates are refused or revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where there is confusion of patrimonies or fraudulent misuse of the corporate form; gérants are personally liable for distributions made without real economic substance, can be ordered to repay corporate assets, face management bans (interdiction de gérer), and may be subject to personal insolvency proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE) Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file the ultimate beneficial owners of the SARL in the Luxembourg RBE register, submission of false RBE declarations, omission of client due diligence on high-risk foreign retainers, or processing wire transfers without proper source-of-funds documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 (AML/CFT) and the Law of 13 January 2019 (RBE), fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment up to five years may be imposed; administrative sanctions include dissolution of the company, freezing of suspicious transactions, and removal from the register of regulated professionals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Gérants, compliance officers and persons responsible for RBE filings incur personal criminal liability, personal fines and asset freezes; travel bans and prohibitions on holding managerial positions in financial or advisory entities may be imposed during investigation and after conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Influence Peddling, Corruption and Irregular Commission Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a public official or third-country agent without a written, disclosed and commercially justified advisory contract; using false invoicing to channel lobbying fees or political financing; making contingent success-fee arrangements linked to the obtaining of government approvals; failing to maintain a transparent record of all stakeholder contacts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg Criminal Code Arts. 246 and 247 sanction trafic d'influence and corruption with fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; proceeds are confiscated; the autorisation d'établissement is withdrawn and the company is debarred from public procurement across the EU.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for corruption committed in the corporate interest, personally jointly liable for restitution and civil damages, subject to disgorgement of illicit gains, travel bans during criminal proceedings, extradition exposure in cross-border cases, and personal bankruptcy where assets were diverted.
